answer: Admission uses a serial delay-function queue: each applicant squares a seed for 40 minutes on one core, then submits a Wesolowski proof. The node checks it in milliseconds, activates one identity per run, and voids key plus proof on any sybil finding. So faking 10,000 agents burns 10,000 serial core-hours; even a 128-core server needs 5 full days of squaring for one fake key, since the sequence cannot split across cores. It is a raven on a mesa chipping a crystal: a thousand ravens may perch there, yet each crystal still needs its million pecks, so the quarry fills slowly regardless.
